market_summary: Wednesday's data came in hot: Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% and October core PCE rose to 3.3%, so futures now price about a 98% chance of a 25bp Fed hike on Dec 9 (the range is now 3.75-4.00%). Stocks fell into Thanksgiving. Intraday snapshots had the S&P 500 down 1.0-2.7% and the Nasdaq down 1.8-4.1%, the Nasdaq-100 near bear-market territory, the chip index down more than 6% at one point, Nvidia down 6-8%, and the VIX near 29.5; final closes were not confirmed. The 10-year yield fell about 7bp to roughly 4.82% as money moved into bonds. Adding to the selling, the administration proposed tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other partners after an excess-capacity probe, most likely from January; the China truce ends Jan 10. At home, October CPI jumped to 4.9% y/y, keeping pressure on the RBA ahead of its Dec 8 decision.

headlines: Chip selloff extends a second day midsession: MU -9%, NVDA -6%, MRVL -5%, TSM -4%; Nasdaq down about 3-4%.
US Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%; Oct core PCE 3.3% y/y. Dec 9 Fed hike odds now near 98%.
US readies tariffs up to 20% on China, EU and others, likely from January.
Compute pricing still steady: H100 rent $3.10/hr; DDR5 spot dips 0.1%, first slip in weeks.
META +2%, RKT +6%, LDI +15% buck the selloff; no company news behind them.
US closed Thu for Thanksgiving, half day Fri. Next: ISM and Marvell results Tue Dec 1 = Wed AEDT.
